why: The 2026-09-09 run was killed by the OS at 02:2x local (exit 1073807364 = DBG_TERMINATE_PROCESS, the PC crash) after 11,102 s. It writes one receipt at exit, so night_factory's stub -- 'exited 1073807364 with no receipt' -- was all that survived. The per-evaluation log did survive; this receipt is rebuilt from it and is NOT a receipt the job wrote.

the_finding.headline: the crashed run rediscovered nothing: 541 of its 541 distinct genomes were already in the earlier run's log
the_finding.cause: both runs used declared seed 20260909 and bank_seed = seed + 1000*gen, so both drew the same window banks, initialised the same population from the same rng and walked the same tree. The second run was a bit-identical replay of the first and died 93 generations BEHIND where the first had already reached (343 vs 436).
the_finding.so_what: the 3.1 hours were not lost to the crash; they were spent before the crash on work already done. A checkpoint alone would only have made the replay resumable. Fixed 2026-09-10: scripts/night_checkpoint.py carries the search across nights (elites forward, bank seeds drawn from outside every seed any night selected on) and night_factory.resolve_run resumes a crashed run under its own number.

not_reconstructable: the archive re-score on an unseen bank (needs the population and rng state the run held only in memory)
headline: RECONSTRUCTED: 1,945 evaluations over 343 generations, 541 distinct genomes -- ALL 541 already present in the 09-08 run's log (overlap 1.000). The night discovered nothing; the search was replaying itself.
verdict: CANNOT DETERMINE from this run, and that is not the crash's fault. FAILED_VARIANT as a SEARCH: overlap 1.000 with the previous run means zero discovery. No archive row can be reconstructed, and none should be -- the run's contribution was nil before it died.
